core.title: Assert SMOKE cases on operator-observable output that proves the acceptance outcome
core.given: A test file whose declared Phase is SMOKE contains a case that makes assertions
core.when: the case's assertions are written or changed
core.then: At least one assertion must check, on an operator-observable channel (a channel an operator can witness the system through, per the profile's observable-channel vocabulary), the externally visible outcome the case claims — the bound acceptance's Then where one is bound — specifically enough that the case turns red if that behavior disappears.
prefer: Read the acceptance's Then first; identify the externally visible consequence that discharges it.

Exercise the real path through the boundary and assert on the operator-observable channels the profile recognizes; a transport-level success indication is only transport evidence — pair it with the acceptance-specific observable witness.
avoid: Asserting only on objects the test built itself — internal, not operator-observable evidence; it proves the constructor works, which is a unit test's job under a SMOKE label.
Treating any observable assertion (e.g. a generic success indication) as sufficient when it does not prove the declared outcome.
Checking internal calls or mocks instead of the resulting system behavior.
unless: The case makes no assertions at all — skipped here; other rules own that.
core.why: The SMOKE label tells the gate real behaviour was exercised, so it must prove something an operator could witness; a self-built object or a bare success indication leaves the acceptance (e.g. the new order being visible) unproven.
evidence: The stack's convention check reports no SMOKE case that makes assertions but touches none of the operator-observable channels.
Reviewer confirms the real path was exercised (a real request or process, not a self-built object or mock).
Reviewer confirms the witness would fail if the bound acceptance behavior regressed (matches the acceptance's Then, not merely 'the system answered').
verification: An automated validator reports a SMOKE case that makes assertions but touches none of the operator-observable channels recognized for the stack; only SMOKE-phase test files are scanned, in the languages the profile scopes for test files (tooling.language_scopes#test_files), and cases with no assertions are skipped (other rules own those).

The observable-channel vocabulary is stack-specific: the core takes it from the profile (idiom.telemetry#observable_channels), and the realization's check recognizes exactly that vocabulary, which also admits other observable channels.
self-constructed object: a value the test built itself; asserting on it proves the constructor works, which is a unit test's job under a SMOKE label.

Division of labour: the automated check recognizes the channel only; merely touching a channel is not semantically enough. Whether the evidence on that channel is acceptance-specific is judged by the agent/reviewer — a clean check result does not establish compliance.
Severity 3, strict disposition: the gate fails on every finding of this rule; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: SMOKE case with assertions but no observable channel
witness does not prove the claimed/bound acceptance outcome

fires: A SMOKE-phase test case asserts only on fields of an object the test built itself.
A SMOKE-phase test case asserts only on internal calls or mocks.
A SMOKE-phase test case asserts only a generic success response while the bound acceptance promises specific visible content (even though the automated check recognizes the channel).
An asserted SMOKE-phase case with no acceptance binding that asserts only on self-built objects.
doesNotFire: A test whose declared Phase is not SMOKE.
A SMOKE case with no assertions at all (owned by other rules).
A SMOKE case asserting acceptance-specific content on an operator-observable channel (per the profile's channel vocabulary).

bunOnly.reason: Names the stack's canonical channel (the real HTTP response and the markup htmx puts in front of the user) and an in-language example; the core keeps the role-level guidance and takes the channel vocabulary from the profile.
In-language example of the self-built-object anti-pattern; the core states the pattern at role level.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is stack-neutral; only the operator-observable channel enumeration is stack data — for this stack the canonical observation is an HTTP response and the markup inside it (what htmx puts in front of the user) — so it moved to the idiom.telemetry#observable_channels profile entry (idiom.markup_kinds covers only markup kinds). The JavaScript/TypeScript test-language activation fact is carried by the profile's tooling.language_scopes#test_files entry (an existing map key covering languages per check scope, including test files): the core keeps no language fact, and its verification records that the check scans test files in the profile's test-file languages, so the instantiated core applies to exactly the same test files. The detector/validator id and finding string, and the in-language prefer/avoid snippets, are realization-only (bunOnly). Severity 3 and strict disposition stay in core verification per the not-profile-keys rule. Core fact values carry no notes (schema), so the facts[3] 'not a prerequisite' and facts[5] 'never exempts' caveats are preserved via fires[2]/fires[3] and then's 'where one is bound'.
